structure.title: Joining the voyage
structure.text: Ishmael's arrival, friendships, and employment establish a shipboard society before its captain's purpose becomes dominant.

structure.title: An expanding pursuit
structure.text: Sailing episodes alternate with whale studies, dramatic scenes, sermons, and speculation. The changing forms enlarge what the hunt can mean.

people.name: Ishmael
people.text: A restless young schoolteacher who goes to sea whenever he feels low, and signs on to a whaling ship out of Nantucket.

people.name: Queequeg
people.text: A tattooed harpooner from a South Sea island, whom Ishmael first fears as a cannibal and soon counts as his closest friend.

people.name: Ahab
people.text: The captain of the Pequod, a grim, eloquent old whaler with an ivory leg, who rarely shows himself on deck at first.

context.title: A working ship
context.text: Whaling involves labour, rank, specialised skills, and financial interests. The crew's everyday work remains present beneath the captain's private purpose.
context.takeaway: The ship contains many reasons for sailing.

context.title: A book of many forms
context.text: Encyclopedic passages and theatrical scenes change the reader's distance from the action. Their apparent digressions are part of the design.
context.takeaway: Notice what a change of form makes possible.

notice.text: Compare Ishmael's curiosity with Ahab's certainty.
notice.why: The two habits offer competing ways to encounter the unknown.
The hunt depends on people whose lives exceed its symbolic meanings.

opening: Ishmael goes to sea because life ashore is making him dangerous company. A whaling voyage promises work, distance, and strangers worth meeting. Then his captain reveals a purpose the crew did not sign up for: Ahab wants the white whale that took his leg. Melville makes room for friendship, filthy jokes, sermons, and astonishing quantities of whale knowledge while a private obsession gathers command of a ship. The men have their own reasons for sailing; their captain intends to give them his.
